subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Should authenticated ACP clients be allowed to repeatedly replay an already-loaded session without a replay-specific throttle, or should bounded ledger replay receive additional availability controls?
rationale: Source inspection disproves the reported arbitrary-query mechanism, but deciding whether repeated authenticated bounded replay is an accepted trusted-operator capability or a security-relevant denial-of-service boundary requires repository security intent.

options.title: Accept current bounded replay
options.body: Document that ACP is an authenticated trusted-client surface and close this report because fixed parameterized lookups plus storage caps are the intended availability boundary.

options.title: Add replay-specific throttling
options.body: Keep identifier-based queries unchanged but rate-limit or serialize repeated `loadSession` replay for already-known sessions and add focused availability tests.

options.title: Require stronger replay budgeting
options.body: Add replay time or event-delivery budgets in addition to throttling if security review finds that a 5,000-event replay can materially block the ACP process.

recommendation.title: Accept current bounded replay
recommendation.body: Document that ACP is an authenticated trusted-client surface and close this report because fixed parameterized lookups plus storage caps are the intended availability boundary.
